correctness.rationale: At fixed positive age the model is a positive multiple of a Gaussian with covariance Σ=2τD. Its log is a+bᵀx−xᵀH x/2 with H=Σ⁻¹ positive definite and b=Hμ. Completing the square recovers μ=H⁻¹b, D=H⁻¹/(2τ), and M=(2π)^(d/2)√det(H⁻¹) exp(a+bᵀH⁻¹b/2). Every such real a,b and SPD H is admissible. Taking logs is injective, and evaluation of these quadratics is injective exactly when its kernel in the full quadratic space is zero: a nonzero kernel vector can perturb any admissible coefficients by a sufficiently small amount without leaving the open negative-definite cone. Rank gives the lower bound and 0,e_i,2e_i,e_i+e_j successively kill all constant, axis and cross terms of a kernel quadratic, proving sharpness in every d≥1. The planar conic wording covers linear zero loci as well, since a line is contained in a degenerate conic. At one unknown-age clock time, keeping τD fixed keeps the entire field fixed for the same center and mass. At two post-release times an unisolvent array gives the two inverse covariance matrices, whose ratio ρ>1 gives t₀=(ρt₁−t₂)/(ρ−1) and then D, μ and M. This is sufficiency, not a two-time minimum or a stability claim. value.rationale: The exact noiseless rank test is a useful implementation guideline, but the asserted mathematics is textbook interpolation of a quadratic after taking logs, followed by covariance scaling. The count is merely the coefficient dimension, the construction is coordinate quadratic interpolation, and the one- and two-time claims are immediate scalar-product identifiability observations once the covariances are known. There is no nonroutine result on sharp multi-time design, constrained sensor geometries or stability in the finding. Better motivation alone would not salvage a distinct scientific claim.
